summary: try/catch lets your program handle an error and keep running. throw reports an error from your own code when a value breaks the rules.
notes: NumberFormatException is a kind of IllegalArgumentException, so its catch must come first.
finally runs every time, whether or not an exception was thrown.
new FileReader() can throw a checked exception, so the compiler makes you catch it or add throws to the method header.
pitfall: Calling new FileReader("missing.txt") with no try/catch causes the compile error: unreported exception FileNotFoundException; must be caught or declared to be thrown.
